paragraphs: References in this report to the "Company," "we," "us" and "our" refer to Plumas Bancorp and its consolidated subsidiary, unless the context indicates otherwise. References to the "Bank" refer to Company's wholly-owned subsidiary, Plumas Bank. References to "Management" refer to the members of the Company's management and references to the "Board of Directors" or the "Board" refer to the Company's Board of Directors.

The Company. Plumas Bancorp is a bank holding company headquartered in Reno, Nevada. Substantially all of the Company's operations are conducted through its subsidiary, Plumas Bank, which is also the principal source of the Company's revenue.

At December 31, 2025, the Company had consolidated assets of $2.2 billion, deposits of $1.8 billion, other liabilities of $168 million and shareholders' equity of $261 million. The Company's other liabilities include $21 million in borrowings, $29 million in lease liabilities and $98 million in repurchase agreements. These items are described in detail later in this Form 10-K.
The Company is a California corporation incorporated in 2002 for the purpose of becoming the holding company for the Bank, which it acquired in a bank holding company reorganization the same year.

Our common stock trades on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the symbol "PLBC." We file annual, quarterly, and other reports required under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC"). These reports are available at no cost on our website, www.plumasbank.com, as soon as reasonably practicable after filing with the SEC. These reports are also available through the SEC's website at www.sec.gov. The address of our headquarters is 5525 Kietzke Lane, Suite 100, Reno, Nevada, 89511.

The Bank. The Bank is a California state-chartered bank that was incorporated and commenced business in 1980. The Bank's deposit accounts are insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (the "FDIC") up to applicable legal limits. The Bank is a member of the Federal Reserve System. At December 31, 2025, the Bank had approximately $2.2 billion in assets, $1.5 billion in net loans and $1.8 billion in deposits (including deposits of $9.4 million from the Company), other liabilities of $146 million and shareholders' equity of $273 million. The Bank's other liabilities include $29 million in lease liabilities and $98 million in repurchase agreements. It is currently the largest bank headquartered in Plumas County, California. The Bank's operations are conducted through its administrative office in Quincy, California.

The Bank primarily generates revenue from loans and investment securities in its portfolio and, to a lesser extent, service fees. With a predominant focus on personal service, the Bank positions itself as a multi-community independent bank serving the financial needs of individuals and businesses within the Bank's geographic footprint. The Bank's primary business is servicing the banking needs of these communities.
Our business has a modest seasonal component due to the heavy agricultural and tourism orientation of some of the communities we serve.

The Bank's primary service area covers the Northeastern portion of California, with Lake Tahoe to the south and the Oregon border to the north, and the Northwestern portion of Nevada. The Bank operates seventeen branches in California, including branches in Alturas, Anderson, Chester, Chico, Fall River Mills, Greenville, Kings Beach, Portola, Quincy, Red Bluff, Redding, Susanville, Tahoe City, Truckee and Yuba City. On July 1, 2025, we acquired our Anderson and Red Bluff branches and two branches in Redding with the acquisition of Cornerstone Community Bank ("Cornerstone"). In December 2015 the Bank opened a branch in Reno, Nevada, its first branch outside of California, and in 2018 the Bank purchased a branch located in Carson City, Nevada.

The Bank maintains 23 automated teller machines ("ATMs") tied in with major statewide and national networks. In addition to its branch network, the Bank operates a lending office specializing in government-guaranteed lending in Auburn, California with an additional lending officer in Southern California, a lending officer in Chandler, Arizona and a commercial/agricultural lending office located in Klamath Falls, Oregon. The Bank's primary business is servicing the banking needs of these communities. Its marketing strategy emphasizes its local ownership and commitment to serve the banking needs of individuals living and working in the Bank's primary service areas.
The Bank's marketing strategy emphasizes its local ownership and management and commitment to serve the banking needs of individuals living and working in the Bank's primary service areas.

Our strategy is to counter rising competition by providing our own style of community-oriented, personalized service. We rely on local promotional activity, personal contacts by our officers, directors, employees, and shareholders, automated 24-hour banking, and the individualized service that we can provide through our flexible policies. This approach appears to be well-received by our customers who appreciate a more personal and customer-oriented environment in which to conduct their financial transactions. To meet the needs of customers who prefer to bank electronically, we offer telephone banking, mobile banking, remote deposit, mobile deposit, and internet banking with bill payment capabilities. This high tech and high touch approach allows customers to tailor their access to our services based on their particular preferences.

The Bank provides Small Business Administration (SBA) loans to qualified borrowers mostly in Northern California, through its government-guaranteed lending center headquartered in Auburn, California. In addition to its Auburn location the Bank has an SBA lender based in each of Atascadero, California and Chandler, Arizona. In 2007 the Bank was granted nationwide Preferred Lender status with the U.S. Small Business Administration,

which enables our customers to obtain SBA funding without the potentially lengthy SBA approval process necessary of lenders than are not SBA Preferred Lenders. We expect government-guaranteed lending to continue to be an important part of our overall lending operation. We offer a SBA 7(a) loan product with a variable interest rate in which the guaranteed portion is salable in the secondary market, but we have seen a significant decline in interest in this product during the last several years. However, we have successfully pivoted to producing fixed rate SBA 7(a) loans, which we generally hold in our loan portfolio.

headings: Risks Relating to our Business and Industry
The majority of our assets are loans, which are subject to credit risks and potential losses.
A deterioration of national or local economic conditions could reduce our profitability.
If our allowance for credit losses is not sufficient to absorb actual loan losses, our profitability could be reduced.
A deterioration in the real estate market could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Inflationary pressures and rising prices may affect our results of operations and financial condition.
Changes in interest rates could reduce our business and profitability.
A lack of liquidity could adversely affect our operations and jeopardize our business, financial condition and results of operations.
A reduction in the value, or impairment of our investment securities, can impact our earnings and common shareholders' equity.
Adverse developments affecting the banking industry may erode customer confidence in the banking system and could have a material effect on our operations and/or stock price.

We could be required to raise additional capital in the future, but that capital may not be available when it is needed or may not be available on terms that are favorable to us or our existing shareholders.
The markets in which we operate are subject to the risks of drought, fires, earthquakes and other natural disasters.
We are subject to market, operational, accounting, credit and other related risks associated with our interest rate hedging strategies.
We face substantial competition from larger banks and other financial institutions.
Our growth strategy involves risks.
Our accounting estimates and risk management processes rely on analytical and forecasting models.
The accuracy of our financial statements and related disclosures could be affected if the judgments, assumptions or estimates used in our critical accounting policies are inaccurate.
Cybersecurity breaches and technological disruptions could damage our reputation and profitability.
Technology is changing rapidly and may put us at a competitive disadvantage.
The use of artificial intelligence in our marketplace may result in reputational harm or liability, or could otherwise adversely affect our business.
We face risks relating to our reliance on third party vendors.
Damage to our reputation could significantly harm our business and prospects.
We are exposed to risk of environmental liabilities with respect to real properties that we may acquire.
Risks Related to Regulation of the Company and the Bank
We are subject to extensive regulation and may face regulatory enforcement actions, incur fines, penalties and other negative consequences from regulatory violations.
Regulatory policies regarding loans secured by commercial real estate could limit our ability to leverage our capital and adversely affect our growth and profitability.
General Risk Factors
The trading price of our common stock may be volatile or may decline.
The trading volume of our common stock is limited.
Our disclosure controls and procedures may not prevent or detect all errors or acts of fraud.
We rely on key executives and personnel and the loss of any of them could have a material adverse impact on our prospects.
Climate change may materially adversely affect our business and results of operations.
paragraphs: The Bank, like other lenders, is subject to credit risk, which is the risk of losing principal or interest due to borrowers' failure to perform their obligations in accordance with the terms of their credit agreements. Underwriting and documentation controls cannot mitigate all credit risk. Accordingly, our results of operations will be directly affected by the volume and timing of loan losses, which for several reasons can vary from period to period. The risks of loan losses may be exacerbated by a downturn in the economy or the real estate market in our market areas or a rapid increase in interest rates, which could have a negative effect on collateral values and borrowers' ability to repay. To the extent borrowers do not timely pay our loans, the loans are placed on non-accrual status, thereby reducing interest income. Further, under these circumstances, we may be required to make an additional provision for loan and lease losses or unfunded commitments, which could reduce our income and capital. See Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations – "Analysis of Asset Quality and Allowance for Credit Losses".

Our lending operations and customers are primarily located in the eastern region of Northern California and in Northern Nevada. As a result, a significant majority of the loans in our loan portfolios as of December 31, 2025, were secured by properties and collateral located within these regions. As of such date, approximately 92% of the loans in our loan portfolio were made to borrowers who primarily conduct business or live in Northern California or Northern Nevada. This geographic concentration imposes risks from lack of geographic diversification, as adverse economic developments in Northern California or Northern Nevada, among other things, could affect the volume of loan originations, increase the level of nonperforming assets, increase the rate of foreclosure losses on loans and reduce the value of our loans and the underlying collateral. Any regional or local economic downturn affecting Northern California or Northern Nevada or existing or prospective borrowers or property values in such areas may affect us and our profitability more significantly and more adversely than depository organizations whose operations are less geographically concentrated. A significant downturn in the national economy or the local economy due to the real estate market, monetary or public policy decisions, tariffs and internal trading tension, agricultural commodity prices, natural disaster, fires, drought or other factors could result in a decline in the local economy in general, which could in turn negatively impact our business, financial condition, results of operations and prospects.

The risk of loan losses is inherent in the lending business. We maintain an allowance for credit losses based upon our actual losses over a relevant time period and management's assessment of all relevant qualitative factors that may cause future loss experience to differ from our historical loss experience. Although we maintain a rigorous process for determining the allowance for credit losses, we cannot be certain that it will be sufficient to cover future loan losses. Determining the appropriate levels of the allowances for credit losses inherently involves a high degree of subjectivity and judgment and requires us to make estimates of current credit risks and future trends, all of which may undergo material changes. If our allowance for credit losses is not adequate to absorb future losses, or if bank regulatory agencies require us to increase our allowance for credit losses, our earnings could be significantly and adversely impacted.

As of December 31, 2025, approximately 77% of our total loan portfolio is secured by real estate, the majority of which is commercial real estate. The market value of real estate can fluctuate significantly in a short period of time as a result of market conditions in the area in which the real estate is located. Adverse changes affecting real estate values and the liquidity of real estate in our markets could increase the credit risk associated with our loan portfolio and could result in losses that would adversely affect credit quality, financial condition, and results of operation. Negative changes in the economy affecting real estate values and liquidity in our market areas could significantly impair the value of property pledged as collateral on loans and affect our ability to sell the collateral upon foreclosure without a loss or additional losses. Collateral may have to be sold for less than the outstanding balance of the loan, which could result in losses on such loans. Declines in real estate market values or increases in commercial and consumer delinquency levels could require increased net charge-offs which could adversely affect our financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

Inflation began to rise sharply at the end of 2021 and has remained at an elevated level through 2024. While some broad inflation rates began to moderate in 2025, inflation rates in some sectors remained elevated relative to historical levels. Small to medium-sized businesses may be impacted more during periods of high inflation as they are not able to leverage economics of scale to mitigate cost pressures compared to larger businesses. Consequently, the ability of our business customers to repay their loans may deteriorate, and in some cases this deterioration may occur quickly, which would adversely impact our results of operations and financial condition. Furthermore, a prolonged period of inflation could cause wages and other costs to the Company to increase, which could adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.

Our earnings could be significantly and adversely impacted by changes in interest rates. While we maintain processes for managing the impact of interest rate fluctuations on earnings, there is a risk that these processes may not fully mitigate the impact of interest rate fluctuations on our business and profitability.

paragraphs: Plumas Bancorp is a bank holding company for Plumas Bank, a California state-chartered commercial bank. We derive our income primarily from interest received on real estate related, commercial, automobile and consumer loans and, to a lesser extent, interest on investment securities and cash balances and fees received in connection with servicing deposit and loan customers. Our major operating expenses are the interest we pay on deposits and borrowings and general operating expenses. We rely on locally-generated deposits to provide us with funds for making loans.

We are subject to competition from other financial institutions and our operating results, like those of other financial institutions operating in California and Northern Nevada, are significantly influenced by economic conditions in California and Northern Nevada, including the strength of the real estate market. In addition, both the fiscal and regulatory policies of the federal and state government and regulatory authorities that govern financial institutions and market interest rates also impact the Bank's financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

On March 28, 2025, Plumas Bank entered into an agreement for the purchase and sale of real property (the "Purchase Agreement"). The Purchase Agreement as amended provided for the sale to BBS Branch III, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, two administrative buildings located in Quincy California for an aggregate cash purchase price of $5.5 million. The sale was completed on November 19, 2025, resulting in a net gain on sale of $5.5 million, recording of right-of-use assets totaling $5.3 million and recording a lease liability of $4.7 million.

Concurrent with the closing of the sale, Plumas Bank and Plumas Investor, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company and Plumas Quincy, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company entered into triple net lease agreements (the "Lease Agreements") pursuant to which the Bank leased back the Properties sold. The Lease Agreements have an initial term of 15 years with three five-year renewal options. The Lease Agreements provide for annual rent of approximately $463,000 in the aggregate for both Properties, increasing by three percent per annum each year.

The gain on sales of the branches was mostly offset by a $5.4 million loss on the sale of approximately $47 million in investment securities. We sold $47 million in investment securities having a weighted average tax equivalent yield of 2.43% recording a $5.4 million loss on the sales. As part of the restructuring, beginning in November 2025 and ending on January 13, 2026, we purchased $42 million in investment securities having a weighted average tax equivalent yield of 4.88%.

On January 19, 2024, Plumas Bank entered into two agreements for the purchase and sale of real property (the "Sale Agreements"). One Sale Agreement provided for the sale to MountainSeed of nine properties owned and operated by Plumas Bank as branches for an aggregate cash purchase price of approximately $25.7 million. The branch portion of the sale was completed on February 14, 2024 resulting in a net gain on sale of $19.9 million, recording of right-of-use assets totaling $22.3 million and recording a lease liability of $22.3 million. The second Sale Agreement provided for the sale to MountainSeed of up to three properties operated as non-branch administrative offices (the "Non-Branch Offices"). This agreement was terminated in August 2024.

Concurrently with the closing of the sale of the branch properties, we entered into triple net lease agreements (the "Lease Agreements") pursuant to which Plumas Bank leased back each of the properties sold. Each Lease Agreement has an initial term of fifteen years with one 15-year renewal option. The Lease Agreements provide for an annual rent of approximately $2.4 million in the aggregate for the nine properties increased by two percent (2%) per annum for each year during the initial Term. During the renewal term, the initial rent will be the basic rent during the last year of the initial term, increased by two percent (2%) per annum for each year during the renewal term.

The gain on sales of the branches was offset by losses on the sale of approximately $115 million in investment securities. We sold $115 million in investment securities having a weighted average tax equivalent yield of 2.24% recording a $19.8 million loss on the sales. As part of the restructuring, beginning in December 2023 and ending on March 27, 2024, we purchased $120 million in investment securities having a weighted average tax equivalent yield of 5.25%.

On July 1, 2025 (the "Closing Date"), Plumas Bancorp (the "Company") completed its previously announced acquisition of Cornerstone Community Bancorp ("Cornerstone") pursuant to an Agreement and Plan of Merger and Reorganization, dated as of January 28, 2025, by and between the Company and Cornerstone (the "Merger Agreement"). Total book value of assets acquired from Cornerstone, excluding fair value adjustments, were $658 million, gross loans totaled $478 million, and deposits totaled $580 million. Goodwill associated with the acquisition of Cornerstone was $18.7 million; the core deposit intangible (CDI) was $11.6 million. In addition, the Company recorded a discount on the acquired loans totaling $15.5 million. With the completion of the merger, Plumas Bank adds four branches in Anderson, Red Bluff and Redding (two branches), California.

Pursuant to the Merger Agreement, on the Closing Date, Cornerstone merged with and into the Company (the "Merger") with the Company continuing as the surviving corporation. Immediately following the Merger, Cornerstone's subsidiary, Cornerstone Community Bank (CCB) merged with and into the Company's subsidiary, Plumas Bank with Plumas Bank as the surviving bank. Pursuant to the terms of the Merger Agreement, upon the completion of the Merger, each share of Cornerstone common stock outstanding immediately prior was converted into the right to receive 0.6608 shares of common stock of the Company and $9.75 cash, with cash paid in lieu of fractional shares. The total aggregate consideration delivered to holders of Cornerstone common stock in the Merger was 1,003,718 shares of Company common stock and $14.8 million cash. In addition, in accordance with the Merger Agreement, the Company paid approximately $1.3 million to holders of options to purchase Cornerstone common stock that were terminated in connection with the Merger. The Company also assumed options to purchase 35,000 shares of Cornerstone common stock representing, on an as-converted basis, options to purchase 30,803 shares of the Company's common stock.

As a result of and upon the completion of the Merger, the Company assumed Cornerstone's obligations with respect to an aggregate principal amount of $12 million of subordinated notes, comprised of (a) $2 million in aggregate principal amount of 4.75% Fixed to Floating Rate Subordinated Notes due November 30, 2035 (the "2035 Notes") and (b) $10 million in aggregate principal amount of 4.75% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Subordinated Notes due November 30, 2030 (the "2030 Notes"). The 2035 Notes, which were issued in 2020, have a fixed interest rate of 4.75% for the first ten years and thereafter a quarterly variable interest rate equal to the then current three-month term Secured Overnight Financing Rate ("SOFR") plus 4.14%. The 2030 Notes, which were issued in 2020, have a fixed interest rate of 4.75% for the first five years and thereafter a quarterly variable interest rate equal to the then current three-month term SOFR plus 4.52%. The 2030 notes were called for redemption on December 30, 2025. Of the $10 million originally outstanding on the 2030 notes, principal payments were made on $5.8 million while $4.2 million remain outstanding at December 31, 2025. The remaining $4.2 million will be paid once the notes are surrendered for cancelation by the debenture holders as required under the 2030 Notes. In accordance with the terms of the 2030 Notes interest has ceased to accrue on the remaining $4.2 million. Interest expense recognized on the subordinated notes for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, was $426 thousand.

Our financial statements are prepared in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (U.S. GAAP). In connection with the acquisition, the Company incurred a variety of non-recurring expenses related to the Merger which are summarized on the following page under the heading "Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Disclosure". The non-recurring expenses for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025 were $7.3 million. Excluding these expenses, non-GAAP net income for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025 would have been $35.0 million, resulting in diluted earnings per share of $5.37 and return on average assets of 1.80%.

In addition, during the second half of 2025, the Company recorded additional expense and income related to the amortization and accretion, respectively related to the amortization/accretion of various Fair Value (FV) marks required under GAAP. The following table presents the effect on pretax earnings of the amortization/accretion of the FV marks recorded during the six months ended December 31, 2025 and the projected effect for the twelve months ended December 31, 2026. Positive numbers would increase pretax income and negative are a decrease in pretax income.

paragraphs: 本報告中提及的 "本公司"、"我們"、"我們" 及 "我們的"，均指 Plumas Bancorp 及其合併子公司，除非文意另有說明。提及 "銀行" 指本公司之 wholly-owned 子公司 Plumas Bank。提及 "管理層" 指本公司之管理層，提及 "董事會" 或 "董事會" 指本公司之董事會。
本公司。Plumas Bancorp 為一家總部設於內華達州雷諾市的銀行控股公司。本公司幾乎所有營運均透過其子公司 Plumas Bank 進行，而 Plumas Bank 亦為本公司主要收入來源。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司合併資產為 2.2 十億美元，存款為 1.8 十億美元，其他負債為 168 百萬美元，股東權益為 261 百萬美元。本公司其他負債包括 21 百萬美元借款、29 百萬美元租賃負債及 98 百萬美元買回協議。這些項目在本 Form 10-K 後續部分有詳細說明。
本公司為一間於 2002 年在加州註冊成立的公司，目的是成為銀行之控股公司，其於同年透過銀行控股公司重組取得銀行。

我們的普通股於納斯達克股票市場交易，代碼為 "PLBC"。我們依證券交易法 1934 年之規定，向證券交易委員會（"SEC"）提交年度、季報及其他報告。這些報告在提交給 SEC 後，盡可能迅速地於我們網站 www.plumasbank.com 上免費提供。這些報告亦可透過 SEC 網站 www.sec.gov 取得。本公司總部地址為 5525 Kietzke Lane, Suite 100, Reno, Nevada, 89511。

銀行。銀行為一間在加州註冊的州立銀行，於 1980 年成立並開始營運。銀行的存款帳戶由美國存款保險公司（"FDIC"）承保，承保額為適用法律之限額。銀行為美國聯邦儲備系統之成員。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，銀行資產約為 2.2 十億美元，淨貸款為 1.5 十億美元，存款為 1.8 十億美元（包括來自本公司之存款 9.4 百萬美元），其他負債為 146 百萬美元，股東權益為 273 百萬美元。銀行其他負債包括 29 百萬美元租賃負債及 98 百萬美元買回協議。目前為加州普盧默斯縣最大之銀行。銀行營運透過其位於加州奎西市之行政辦公室進行。
銀行主要收入來自其投資組閤中的貸款及投資證券，其次為服務費用。以個人服務為主導，銀行定位為一家服務多個社區之獨立銀行，滿足其服務範圍內個人及企業之金融需求。銀行主要業務為服務這些社區之銀行需求。
我們的業務因部分服務社區具有濃厚農業及旅遊產業特性，而具有一點季節性影響。

本銀行的主要服務區域涵蓋加州的東北部，南至湖塔霍（Lake Tahoe），北至俄勒岡州邊界，以及內華達州的西北部。本銀行在加州經營十七家分行，包括位於艾爾塔uras、安德森（Anderson）、切斯特（Chester）、奇科（Chico）、法爾河 Mills、格林維爾（Greenville）、金斯湖（Kings Beach）、波托拉（Portola）、奎西（Quincy）、紅崖（Red Bluff）、紅ding、蘇珊維爾（Susanville）、塔霍城（Tahoe City）、特魯克（Truckee）及葉巴城（Yuba City）的分行。於2025年7月1日，我們透過收購Cornerstone Community Bank（"Cornerstone"）取得安德森（Anderson）與紅崖（Red Bluff）分行，以及紅ding的兩家分行。2015年12月，本銀行在內華達州雷諾（Reno）開設第一家位於加州以外的分行，並於2018年購入位於卡森城（Carson City）的分行。

本銀行維繫23臺自動提款機（"ATMs"），與主要的州內及全國性網路連結。除了分行網路外，本銀行在加州 Auburn 運營專門從事政府擔保貸款的貸款辦公室，並在南加州設有額外貸款經理，亞利桑那州錢德勒（Chandler）設有貸款經理，以及位於俄勒岡州克萊馬斯瀑布（Klamath Falls）的商業/農業貸款辦公室。本銀行的主要業務是服務這些社區的銀行需求。其行銷策略強調本地所有權及對服務這些社區居民的承諾。
本銀行的行銷策略強調其本地所有權及管理，並對服務這些社區居民的承諾。

我們的策略是透過提供我們獨特的社區導向、個人化服務來對抗日益激烈的競爭。我們依賴本地宣傳活動、高層、董事、員工及股東的個人接觸、24小時自動銀行服務，以及透過我們靈活政策所提供的個性化服務。這種方式似乎受到客戶的歡迎，他們欣賞一個更個人化、以客戶為導向的環境來進行財務交易。為滿足偏好電子銀行的客戶需求，我們提供電話銀行、行動銀行、遠距存款、行動存款及網際網路銀行服務，並具備帳單支付功能。這種高科技與高接觸的模式，使客戶能根據個人偏好調整對我們服務的存取方式。

本銀行透過位於加州 Auburn 的政府擔保貸款中心，為符合資格的借款人提供小企業管理局（Small Business Administration, SBA）貸款，主要在北加州地區。除了 Auburn 之外，本銀行在加州阿塔斯克德羅（Atascadero）及亞利桑那州錢德勒（Chandler）也設有 SBA 貸款經理。2007 年，本銀行獲得了美國小企業管理局（U.S. Small Business Administration）全國 Preferred Lender 資格，

這使我們的客戶能在不需經歷非 SBA Preferred Lender 借款人可能需要的潛在漫長 SBA 批准程序的情況下，取得 SBA 資金。我們預期政府擔保貸款將持續成為我們整體貸款業務的重要組成部分。我們提供一種 SBA 7(a) 貸款產品，利率為變動利率，其中擔保部分可在二級市場出售，但我們在過去幾年中觀察到對此產品的興趣顯著下降。然而，我們已成功轉型為提供固定利率的 SBA 7(a) 貸款，我們通常將這些貸款納入貸款組閤中。

paragraphs: Plumas Bancorp 為 Plumas Bank 的銀行控股公司，Plumas Bank 為位於加州的州立商業銀行。我們的收入主要來自於與不動產相關、商業、汽車及消費貸款所收取的利息，以及較少程度的投資證券及現金餘額利息，以及為存款及貸款客戶提供服務所收取的費用。我們的主要營運費用為支付存款及借款的利息，以及一般營運費用。我們依賴當地產生的存款，以提供資金用於貸款。
我們面臨來自其他金融機構的競爭，且我們的營運成果，如同其他在加州及內華達州北部營運的金融機構一樣，受到加州及內華達州北部總體經濟條件的顯著影響，包括不動產市場的強弱。此外，聯邦及州政府及監管機構針對金融機構及市場利率所制定的財政與監管政策，也影響銀行的財務狀況、營運成果及現金流。

2025 年 3 月 28 日，Plumas Bank 與 BBS Branch III, LLC 籤訂買賣不動產的協議（"買賣協議"）。經修正後的買賣協議，同意以總計 5.5 百萬美元現金出售位於加州奎西市的兩棟行政大樓給 BBS Branch III, LLC，這是一家特拉華州有限責任公司。買賣於 2025 年 11 月 19 日完成，產生淨售出收益 5.5 百萬美元，記錄總計 5.3 百萬美元的使用權資產，並記錄 4.7 百萬美元的租賃負債。
與買賣完成同時，Plumas Bank 與 Plumas Investor, LLC，一家特拉華州有限責任公司，以及 Plumas Quincy, LLC，一家特拉華州有限責任公司簽訂三重淨租賃協議（"租賃協議"），根據這些協議，銀行租回已出售的不動產。租賃協議的初始租期為 15 年，並有三個 5 年的續約選擇權。租賃協議規定，兩處不動產的年度租金總計約為 463,000 美元，每年增加 3%。
出售分行的收益大部分被出售約 47 百萬美元投資證券所產生的 5.4 百萬美元損失所抵銷。我們出售了總計 47 百萬美元投資證券，加權平均稅後等效收益率為 2.43%，產生 5.4 百萬美元的損失。作為重組的一部分，自 2025 年 11 月開始，至 2026 年 1 月 13 日結束，我們購買了總計 42 百萬美元投資證券，加權平均稅後等效收益率為 4.88%。

2024 年 1 月 19 日，Plumas Bank 與 MountainSeed 籤訂兩份買賣不動產的協議（"買賣協議"）。其中一份買賣協議規定，以總計約 25.7 百萬美元現金出售 Plumas Bank 所擁有並營運的九處分行不動產給 MountainSeed。分行部分的買賣於 2024 年 2 月 14 日完成，產生淨售出收益 19.9 百萬美元，記錄總計 22.3 百萬美元的使用權資產，並記錄 22.3 百萬美元的租賃負債。第二份買賣協議規定，出售至多三處作為非分行行政辦公室（"非分行辦公室"）的不動產給 MountainSeed。此協議於 2024 年 8 月終止。
與出售分行不動產的買賣同時，我們簽訂三重淨租賃協議（"租賃協議"），根據這些協議，Plumas Bank 租回每處已出售的不動產。每份租賃協議的初始租期為十五年，並有一個 15 年的續約選擇權。租賃協議規定，九處不動產的年度租金總計約為 2.4 百萬美元，每年增加 2%（2%）於初始租期內的每個年度。在續約期間，初始租金將為初始租期最後一年的基本租金，並於續約期間的每個年度增加 2%（2%）。
出售分行的收益被出售約 115 百萬美元投資證券所產生的損失所抵銷。我們出售了總計 115 百萬美元投資證券，加權平均稅後等效收益率為 2.24%，產生 19.8 百萬美元的損失。作為重組的一部分，自 2023 年 12 月開始，至 2024 年 3 月 27 日結束，我們購買了總計 120 百萬美元投資證券，加權平均稅後等效收益率為 5.25%。

於 2025 年 7 月 1 日（「交易日」），Plumas Bancorp（「本公司」）完成其先前宣佈的收購 Cornerstone Community Bancorp（「Cornerstone」）交易，依據 2025 年 1 月 28 日由本公司與 Cornerstone 簽訂之合併與重組協議（「合併協議」）。排除公平價值調整後，從 Cornerstone 收購取得的資產總帳面價值為 658 百萬美元，總貸款金額為 478 百萬美元，存款總額為 580 百萬美元。與收購 Cornerstone 相關的商譽為 18.7 百萬美元；核心存款無形資產（CDI）為 11.6 百萬美元。此外，本公司針對取得的貸款記錄了 15.5 百萬美元的折價。隨著合併完成，Plumas Bank 新增了位於 Anderson、Red Bluff 與 Redding（兩家分行）的四家分行，位於加利福尼亞州。

根據合併協議，於交易日，Cornerstone 合併進本公司（「合併」），本公司繼續為存續公司。合併後立即，Cornerstone 的子公司 Cornerstone Community Bank（CCB）合併進本公司子公司 Plumas Bank，Plumas Bank 為存續銀行。根據合併協議的條款，合併完成後，每持有 Cornerstone 普通股一股，將轉換為取得本公司普通股 0.6608 股及現金 9.75 美元，現金用以代替小數股。合併中交付給 Cornerstone 普通股持有人的總對價為 1,003,718 本公司普通股及 14.8 百萬美元現金。此外，根據合併協議，本公司支付約 1.3 百萬美元給持有 Cornerstone 普通股選擇權的持有人，這些選擇權因合併而終止。本公司也承擔了購買 35,000 份 Cornerstone 普通股選擇權，換算成本公司普通股為 30,803 份。

由於並於合併完成後，本公司承擔 Cornerstone 對於總本金金額為 12 百萬美元的次級債券的義務，包含（a）總本金金額為 2 百萬美元的 4.75% 固定至浮動利率次級債券，到期日為 2035 年 11 月 30 日（「2035 債券」）及（b）總本金金額為 10 百萬美元的 4.75% 固定至浮動利率次級債券，到期日為 2030 年 11 月 30 日（「2030 債券」）。2035 債券於 2020 年發行，前十年固定利率為 4.75%，其後每季變動利率為當時三個月期 secured overnight financing rate（「SOFR」）加上 4.14%。2030 債券於 2020 年發行，前五年固定利率為 4.75%，其後每季變動利率為當時三個月期 SOFR 加上 4.52%。2030 債券於 2025 年 12 月 30 日被要求贖回。於 2030 債券原 10 百萬美元中，已償還 5.8 百萬美元本金，餘下 4.2 百萬美元於 2025 年 12 月 31 日仍為未償還。剩餘 4.2 百萬美元將在債券持有人依 2030 債券條款將債券繳回銷毀後支付。根據 2030 債券條款，剩餘 4.2 百萬美元的利息已停止計息。2025 年 12 月 31 日前十二個月，與次級債券相關的利息費用為 426 千美元。

本公司財務報表係依美國通用會計準則（U.S. GAAP）編製。與收購相關，本公司產生多種非經常性費用，與合併有關，詳見下頁標題為「非 GAAP 披露明細」的說明。2025 年 12 月 31 日前十二個月的非經常性費用為 7.3 百萬美元。扣除這些費用後，2025 年 12 月 31 日前十二個月的非 GAAP 稅後淨利為 35.0 百萬美元，每股稀釋收益為 5.37 美元，平均資產回報率為 1.80%。
此外，於 2025 年第二季，本公司記錄與公平價值（FV）標記相關的額外費用與收入，這些費用與收入係根據 GAAP 要求的公平價值標記的攤銷與計息。下表顯示 2025 年 12 月 31 日前六個月及預計 2026 年 12 月 31 日前十二個月，公平價值標記的攤銷/計息對預稅淨利的影響。正數會增加預稅淨利，負數則會減少預稅淨利。

paragraphs: 本銀行，如同其他貸款機構，面臨信用風險，即因借款人未能依照信用協議的條款履行其義務，而導致本金或利息損失的風險。授信與文件控管程序無法完全降低信用風險。因此，我們的營運成果將直接受到貸款損失的數量與發生時間的影響，而貸款損失的數量與發生時間可能因多種原因而於不同期間有所差異。貸款損失的風險可能因我們營運地區的經濟或不動產市場出現衰退，或利率快速上升而更加嚴重，這可能會對擔保價值與借款人償還貸款的能力產生負面影響。若借款人未能及時償還貸款，該貸款將被列為非應計貸款，從而減少利息收入。此外，在這種情況下，我們可能需要增加貸款與租賃貸款及未資金承諾的撥備，這可能會減少我們的收入與資本。請參閱管理層對財務狀況與營運成果的討論與分析 – 「資產品質與信用損失撥備分析」。

我們的貸款業務與客戶主要位於美國北加州東部與內華達州北部。因此，截至2025年12月31日，我們貸款組閤中的貸款，大部分是以位於這些地區的財產與擔保品為抵押。截至該日期，我們貸款組閤中約有92%的貸款是提供給主要業務或居住地在北加州或內華達州北部的借款人。這種地理集中性會帶來缺乏地理分散化的風險，因北加州或內華達州北部的經濟不利發展，或其他因素，可能影響貸款發放的數量，增加非表現不良資產的水準，增加貸款的法拍損失率，並降低我們貸款與擔保品的價值。任何影響北加州或內華達州北部的區域或地方經濟衰退，或影響現有或潛在借款人的經濟狀況或該地區的不動產價值，可能會對我們與我們的獲利造成更顯著且更嚴重的負面影響。若因不動產市場、貨幣或公共政策決策、關稅與內部貿易緊張關係、農產品價格、天然災害、火災、乾旱或其他因素導致國家或地方經濟出現重大衰退，可能會導致該地區整體經濟衰退，進而對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運成果與前景產生負面影響。

貸款損失的風險是貸款業務內在的。我們根據過去一段期間的實際損失與管理層對所有可能導致未來損失經驗與歷史損失經驗不同的質性因素的評估，來維持信用損失撥備。雖然我們維持嚴謹的程序來決定信用損失撥備，但我們無法確定該撥備是否足夠覆蓋未來的貸款損失。決定信用損失撥備的適當水準，本質上涉及高度的主觀性與判斷，並需要我們對目前的信用風險與未來趨勢做出估計，而這些估計可能出現重大變動。若我們的信用損失撥備不足以吸收未來的損失，或若銀行監管機構要求我們提高信用損失撥備，則我們的獲利可能會受到顯著且負面的影響。

截至2025年12月31日，我們總貸款組合約有77%是以不動產為抵押，其中絕大多數為商業不動產。不動產的市場價值可能在短時間內因該不動產所在地區的市場條件而大幅波動。影響不動產價值與不動產流動性的不利變化，可能會增加我們貸款組合的信用風險，並可能導致損失，進而對信用品質、財務狀況與營運成果產生負面影響。影響我們營運地區不動產價值與流動性的經濟不利變化，可能會顯著降低用作貸款擔保品的財產價值，並影響我們在法拍時無損出售該擔保品的能力。擔保品可能必須以低於貸款餘額的價格出售，這可能會導致這些貸款產生損失。不動產市場價值下跌或商業與消費者違約率上升，可能會導致增加淨核銷金額，進而對我們的財務狀況、營運成果與現金流產生負面影響。

通貨膨脹自2021年底開始劇烈上升，並持續維持在高水準至2024年。雖然部分廣義通貨膨脹率在2025年開始緩和，但某些產業的通貨膨脹率仍相較歷史水準維持在高水準。小型至中型企業在高通貨膨脹期間可能受到較大影響，因其無法利用規模經濟來緩解成本壓力，與大型企業相比。因此，我們的業務客戶償還貸款的能力可能會惡化，且在某些情況下，這種惡化可能迅速發生，這將對我們的營運成果與財務狀況產生負面影響。此外，持續的通貨膨脹期間可能會導致本公司的人工成本及其他成本上升，這可能會對我們的營運成果與財務狀況產生負面影響。
我們的獲利可能因利率變動而受到顯著且負面的影響。雖然我們維持管理利率變動對獲利影響的程序，但這些程序可能無法完全抵消利率變動對我們業務與獲利的影響。
